### The problem: traps per width and radius

A property of the problem alone, by enumeration on the true means (3600 points). Certified single points: sets of one point that PyMOSO's certificate would accept at that radius (the efficient set's own points included). First-objective local minima: points no neighbour within the radius is strictly better than, the traps of a single-objective search. Ties: pairs of points in different cells with equal true values.

### Quality at matched counted simulations

The tester-style metric (Hausdorff distance between the true images of the returned set and of the efficient set), or for R-SPLINE the gap to the true minimum of the first objective: lower is better. Median, then seeds better / same / worse than width 1 (the control, no plateaus) on the same seed, solver, radius and arm. "-": no iteration finished by that checkpoint.

### What the search does on a plateau

Per run, medians over seeds (sums of moves over all seeds in brackets). PLI calls, and the share whose pseudo-gradient was exactly zero. Moves by SPLI and by NE that lowered the true value of the objective being searched ("true") against moves that lowered only its estimate ("noise"); NE moves to a point of the same cell, a true tie. Distinct cells the search moved into, and cells in the final returned set. Not for ExampleBnBSolver, which has no PLI, SPLI or NE.
